intro.t: Warm sand under your back. A bassline you can feel in your teeth. Something is blocking the sun.
Hey. Hey. Do not try to sit up. You will only make the sky move.
A face hangs over you, haloed by the light. White beard. Kind eyes. Pupils like dinner plates.
You are dreaming, probably. Good. That makes this easier. Listen.
This festival is not only people. It is full of Astrals: what a state of mind looks like when it gets loose.
That one is a Wooklet. Harmless. Mostly hair. Every mood at this party has a creature like it, somewhere.
People keep them as friends. People battle with them. Nobody here fights with fists any more. Too much effort.
Wear a wild one down in battle, then stabilise it in a baggie. That is how you make friends here.
Look after your team. Hydration is their stamina. Serotonin is their health. Run out and they crash.
There is a blotter in your fanny pack. Lick a corner (L, or LICK on a phone) and the festival opens up: rarer Astrals, bigger lessons. Harder hits, clumsier hands. Water brings you down.
Eight festival bosses hand out Wristbands of Enlightenment. With all eight, the VIP Shaman Council will see you.
Now. Who are you, in there?
{player}. Of course. You look like a {player}.
Any questions?
Real enough to owe me for the coconut water.
Of course it is. The question is whose.
With your passport, I expect. Wherever that is.
Sleep it off, {player}. When you can stand, come and find me by the shack.
4:00 PM. You wake up face-down in the sand.
Your backpack is gone. So are your shoes. So, you slowly realise, is your passport.
In their place: a fanny pack, half a bottle of warm coconut water, and a headache shaped like a bassline.
An old man with a white beard is watching you from the shack. You are almost sure you have met him before.

banyan.t: Ah, you are alive. Good. I am Banyan. I came to Goa in 1994 for two weeks.
You were talking in your sleep, {player}. Astrals, baggies, wristbands. Good. Saves me the speech.
How do I know your name? You told me. You were very chatty for someone unconscious.
Your passport is with the VIP Shaman Council at the Mainstage Temple. To get in you need all 8 Wristbands of Enlightenment.
You will not last an hour alone. Here, I found my stash. Three Astrals. Take one.
Which one calls to you?
Ganjapod. A sleepy coconut. Slow, sturdy, and it heals itself on the couch. Sure?
Jawling. A gecko that never stops talking. Fast and fragile. Sure?
Blottertot. A paper frog. Strange powers, and it bends the rules. Sure?
Good. Now, wild Astrals drift out of the incense clouds. Wear one down, then stabilise it in one of these.
And fill your Trip Journal. Come and show me now and then. I pay in snacks.
Watch its Hydration. Every move costs water, and a parched Astral can only dry heave.
One more thing, and it matters. Out here everything gets you a little high: every fight, every snack, the air.
There are four levels: Microdose, Come-up, Peaking and Ego gone. When you are past a Microdose, the corner of your eye tells you which.
Higher means more Vibes from every fight, rarer Astrals, and baggies that hold better.
But your hands get clumsy, wild Astrals hit harder, and a whiteout costs you more.
That blotter in your fanny pack takes you up fast. Water, chai or a nap bring you down. How high to fly is your call.
Careful, though: stand around with nothing to do and you will start licking it out of boredom. Everybody does. Keep moving.
In a hurry? Hold B and run. Everyone at this festival is in a hurry. Nobody knows where to.
The Chai Mama tent heals everything. The first wristband is with DJ Diabolo at the Poi Pit, north along the trail. I have taken the festival tape down for you: off you go.
Ten Astrals in your Journal already! Here, wraps for the next ten.
Twenty! When I was your age I had seen two, and one of them was a cloud.
Thirty. You are filling that Journal faster than I fill a chillum. Chai for the road.
Every single one. The whole state of mind of this festival, in one duct-taped notebook. I think I can finally go home. I will not, but I could.
DJ Diabolo. Poi Pit. North. Catch a few Astrals on the way, one is never enough.
A wristband already! In 1994 it took me... well. I never got one. Keep going.

sign_beach.t: DRIFTWOOD SHACK BEACH. North: Sandy Trail. Lost property: no.
DRIFTWOOD SHACK BEACH. North: Sandy Trail. The letters are breathing. Lost property: you.

sign_trail.t: SANDY TRAIL. One plank bridge over the creek, no lifeguard. Mind the incense clouds: things come out of them.

beach_hippie.t: The Chai Mama tent over there fixes everything. Serotonin, hydration, the feeling that your hands are too big.
If your whole party fades out you white out, and wake up there six hours later with lighter pockets.
Whoa. Your aura is doing the thing. You can see the stranger by the water now, right? Say hi from me.

beach_tourist.t: I only came for a yoga retreat. That was in March. What month is it?
Is it me, or is that crab talking? It says the month is irrelevant. I think it is right.

chai_tent.t: Sit, drink, sleep it off. Or see to the friends you left with me.
Here is watermelon and a heavy blanket.
There. Your party is rested and watered. Do not tell me what you saw.
You look like you are waiting for something. Sleep here until the next set?

chai_tent_closed.t: Not while {boss} is still on, beta. Everyone who walks in mid-set wants a blanket and a second go.
Win first. Then sit, and I will pour.

chai_tent_gauntlet.t: You started the climb, beta. The Four are waiting upstairs, and they do not wait warm.
You started. Finish, then sit, and I will pour.

shop_closed.t: But the shutters stay down while {boss} is on. House rule: nothing sold mid-set. Come back after.

beach_vendor.t: Baggies, water, balm. Good price, my friend. Festival price.

trail_yogi.t: The fire was here before the festival. So was I. Sit, if you like. The logs do not mind.
If somebody locks eyes with you out here, there is no walking away. Wraparound shades help. So does looking at your feet.

sign_pit.t: THE POI PIT. Resident: DJ Diabolo (set time: ongoing).

pit_vendor.t: You made it to the Pit! Same stock, same price. Maybe a little more.

pit_hippie.t: Diabolo will not even look at you unless you walk right up on stage and talk to him.
You made his record skip! With that wristband, just walk into the fairy lights up north.

pit_local.t: Every type hits two others hard and bounces off two others. Stimulant flattens Organic and Downer. Check your Journal.

sign_yurt.t: THE TANTRIC YURT. Shoes off. Ego off. East: Anjuna Flea Market.

yurt_tourist.t: I paid for a ten-day retreat. On day two she told me I was already enlightened and kept the money.

sign_market.t: ANJUNA FLEA MARKET. North: Clogged Dirt Road. East: Omelette Stall. South: Dry Ice Corridor (VIP).

market_vendor.t: Everything a traveller needs! Papers, sachets, shades, catalysts. I also have a cousin who sells carpets.

market_lassi.t: Catalysts change certain Astrals when they drink them. Lassi for the sleepy ones, Kingfisher for the sunburned, powder for the glowing.

market_guard.t: Road north is closed. Guru Svetlana decides who passes. Her yurt is west.
The Guru vouched for you. Bring a light, it is black as a speaker cone up there.
Pupils like that, at this hour? I am not even going to ask. Do not lick the barrier.

market_hippie.t: A Team Undercover memo! They write everything down. There will be more: try the guesthouse, the villa on the cliff, and the green room backstage.
Bring me all three and we can show the whole festival what they are planning.
All three. Buy the beds, fence the sunset, cut the power to every free party. That is the whole plan, in their own handwriting.
I will pin copies in every Chai Tent from here to Arambol. Take this, from all of us.
The memos are up in every Chai Tent and the fence on the cliff came down. They say the sunset itself comes out to look now, if you go at sunset, and go high.
Team Undercover are all over the market. Guards on the take, dealers selling oregano, influencers fencing off the sunset.
They want to bottle the whole festival's dopamine and shut the free party down.
If you ever find their paperwork, bring it to me. They write everything down.
Your pupils are the size of the problem. Team Undercover would bottle that. Keep moving.

market_tourist.t: The time of day changes what comes out of the incense. I only ever see mosquitoes. I think that is just Goa.
You see them too? The Astrals behind the Astrals? I thought it was just the mosquitoes.

market_wook.t: That subwoofer in the gap is way too heavy. Captain Keta could shift it. If he could find it.
Push it right through, friend. It rolls back when nobody is looking.

market_tuktuk.t: Tuk-tuk? Very cheap. But only for press. You have a press pass? No? Then you walk.
Press pass! Open your Fanny Pack and choose Tuk-tuk. I take you to any Chai Tent you have rested at.

sign_road.t: CLOGGED DIRT ROAD. A sacred cow has been lying across it since Tuesday, and nobody is going to argue. Detours: west by the Jungle Shortcut (one plank, mind the stream), or east by the Roadside Shrine (one gate). No lights. No refunds.
CLOGGED DIRT ROAD. Somebody has crossed out CLOGGED and written underneath in chalk: SHE GOT UP. Under that, in another hand: FOR NOW.

sign_ditch.t: THE SUNKEN SCOOTER DITCH. Captain Keta presiding, approximately.

ditch_wook.t: The sea goes to the lake, and the lake goes to the forest stage. You would need to float though.
You have the cheese stamp! Just walk into the shallows with something Dissociative.

sign_stall.t: THE 5 AM OMELETTE STALL. Open at 5 AM. It is always 5 AM.

stall_local.t: Raju's kitchen is all Organic and Downer. Stimulants cut through both. So does Psychedelic, a little.

sign_sea.t: ARABIAN SEA SHALLOWS. East: Sweetwater Lake. North: the Sadhu Cave (by appointment).

sea_sadhu.t: Baba Smoke sees nobody without a press pass. He says the last blogger got his good side wrong.
A press pass. Go in. Mind your head, and your sense of self.

sign_lake.t: ARAMBOL SWEETWATER LAKE. South: 190 BPM Forest Stage. Earplugs advised.

lake_local.t: Things swim in the lake that do not swim anywhere else. Float out on the water and see.

sign_forest.t: 190 BPM FOREST STAGE. Resident: Baron Von Darkpsy. No requests. Especially not that one.

forest_wook.t: His Astrals are Bummer and Psychedelic. Downers put both to sleep. I would know. I am one.

sign_cliff.t: THE SUNSET CLIFF. This sunset is brought to you by a brand partner.

cliff_tourist.t: A man in a uniform is charging people to look west. He says he has a permit.
The sunset is free again! It was always free. That is rather the point of it.

sign_cave.t: Scratched underneath: 'Something turns in the east wall. It notices you noticing it.'

mandalord.t: A pattern in the rock. It is turning, very slowly. It has noticed you noticing it.
The pattern folds back into the rock. It is still in there. Leave the cave, come back, and it will be turning again.
The rock is just rock now. The pattern is in your Journal, still turning.
You back away. It does not mind. It has time.

shadowcop_bribe.t: A shape made of torch beams blocks the fog. A whistle blows somewhere. It rubs two fingers together.
The beams dim, satisfied. Something small and sheepish drifts out of the light.
You pat your pockets. Not enough. The shape takes this personally.
The shape swells with indignation. It is growing. It has a hat now.

sign_backstage.t: BACKSTAGE CONTAINER. If you can read this you should not be here.

backstage_bar.t: Backstage bar. Artist prices. You are not an artist, so double.

backstage_roadie.t: The Promoter carries one of everything. No type will save you. Bring a full party and a lot of water.

sign_temple.t: MAINSTAGE TEMPLE. The Four-on-the-Floor hold the four doors. Rest at the tent first. There is no tent past the first door.

temple_local.t: Kick, bass, hat, lead. Heavy, wobbly, fast, clever. Then whoever is sulking in the last doorway.

council.t: So. The barefoot one. Eight wristbands, four doors, and one very well dressed ego, all behind you.
You came for a passport. We have had it the whole time. It fell out of your pocket on the beach. We kept it safe.
We could have just handed it back. But then you would have gone home on Tuesday with a clean shirt and no stories.
Your return flight left six days ago. Or it leaves tomorrow. Time is not our department.
You look at the passport. You look at your feet. You have not worn shoes in a week.
A sensible choice. Banyan made the same one in 1994. He is still packing.
Two more weeks. Yes. That is what they all say. That is what we said.
Ah, you are back. With a passport! Put it somewhere safe. Not too safe.
The festival goes on. Your Journal still has blank pages, and there is something in the Sadhu Cave that has been watching for a very long time.
Still here? Good. So are we.

glow_stranger.t: You can see me? Then you are high enough to listen.
The Astrals that hide from sober people come out now. The two creatures Banyan did not give you wander these trails, for those who look while peaking.
Take these. Your hands will shake. Vials forgive shaking.
Banyan's three. One of them came to you on the beach. The other two only show themselves to people who are peaking.
Bag all three and come back to me. High, ideally. I am hard to find otherwise.
All three. You have seen what the festival keeps for the ones who look properly.
This one only lives for thirty seconds at a time. It wants to spend them with you.
Water brings you down. A Chai Tent brings you all the way down. The blotter brings you back up. Choose.

astral_auntie.t: Beta, your aura is leaking all over my stall. Here. Wraps for shaky hands.
When the ego goes, so does your grip. And your wallet, if you white out. Peaking is the sweet spot.

shack_hammock.t: You lie down in Banyan's hammock for a minute. It smells of incense and 1994.
Your Astrals are rested. If you white out, you will wake up here.

shack_diary.t: Banyan's diary, open at a page from 1994: 'Day 3. Two weeks is not enough.' The next page: 'Day 9000. Still not enough.'
Underneath, in newer ink: 'The blotter shows what hides. The Stranger by the water only talks to people who are peaking.'
A bottle of masala chai is wedged in as a bookmark. Banyan would want you to have it.
'Day 9001. A kid washed up on the beach talking about wristbands in their sleep. Gave them my old stash.'
On the last page, a drawing of a turning pattern and the words: 'Sadhu Cave. East wall. Do not stare. It stares back.'
A page you have never seen before, right in the middle of the diary. The ink is still moving.
'Day 4. J. went north with the sadhus to find the room behind the pattern. Said: wait for me at the sunrise set, I will be back before the last track.'
'Day 5. Waited. Day 6. Waited. Day 30. The sunrise set is very beautiful. I will keep coming.'
You blink, and the page is gone. The diary goes straight from Day 3 to Day 9000.

guest_host.t: Sunrise Guesthouse. Beds for the broken, Rs 100 a nap.
You sleep like a rock. Your Astrals do too. You wake up sober and slightly ashamed.
No money, no mattress. The Chai Tent is free, beta.
The noticeboard is for guests. Everyone is a guest. That is the problem.

guest_board.t: NOTICEBOARD. 'Lost: one pair of sandals, very sentimental. Ask the tourist in the corner.'
'Rooms not for rent to Team Undercover.' Someone has crossed out the word 'not'.

guest_tourist.t: I lost my sandals somewhere on the Sandy Trail. They were a gift from my ex. Not the ex. The other one.
If you find them I will pay you. I will pay you so much. I will pay you a reasonable amount.
My sandals! You found them! The hair tie is still there! I could cry. I am crying.
Where is the poncho? Somebody walked off with it while you were out? Festival people.
Here. I bought two. I always buy two of everything. That is how I ended up with two exes.
I am never taking them off again. I am going to sleep in them.

temple_water.t: Halfway up the temple and you look like a raisin. Drink. All of you.
The jug is empty, beta. The Chai Tent downstairs still pours.

pit_spinner.t: Six hours of spinning fire and nobody has brought me a drink. Not one coconut. My mouth is a desert.
Two coconut waters. That is all I ask. The beach stall sells them.
Is that coconut water? Two of them? You beautiful human.
Here. I found it in the ashes. It brings luck, or at least it has a hole in it.
Hydrated and spinning. Watch the eyebrows.

market_collector.t: I collect moods. I have every kind of high in my notebook, but I have never seen a proper Downer up close.
Bring one along in your party and let me look. I will make it worth your while.
Oh. Oh, look at it. So heavy. So unbothered. It has not checked its phone in a year.
Take this. A friend made it for me. Your friends should have one too.
My notebook is complete. I am now collecting naps.

booth_roadie.t: Someone nicked our record crates and dumped them around the jungle. The stage, the bamboo, the lake. Three of them.
No crates, no closing set. Bring them back and the Selector will owe you one.
All three crates! You found them! Hand them over and the set goes on.
A dealer at the market would pay well for rare vinyl. Nobody would know.
Legend. The Selector says this is yours. It makes everything louder, including you.
Only two came back? Fine. FINE. The closing set will be... short.
Later, a dealer pays you for the crate you kept. It feels exactly as good as you expected.
Best closing set of the season. You are on the guest list forever.
The set was short. Somebody's crate went missing. I am not saying it was you. I am looking at you, though.

sunraga.t: The sun stops halfway into the sea. Then it turns round and looks at you.
Nobody has fenced it off. Nobody is selling tickets. It seems relieved.
The sun drops into the sea after all. It will be back. It always is, at sunset, for the ones who are high enough to see it.
For the first time all week the sunset is free. Some of it is in your Journal now.
You back away. It does not mind. It has time.

bassilisk.t: The speaker stack is humming a note too low to hear. The floor hears it. Your teeth hear it.
The bass sinks back into the speakers. Walk out, walk back in, and it will be humming again.
The speakers fall quiet. The whole of Backstage feels lighter. The bass is in your Journal, still humming.
You back away. It does not mind. It has time.

sunset_watcher.t: I come here every evening. Since Chloe fenced it off I watch the sunset through the gaps.
Sit with me until it goes down?
You sit on the warm rock. The hours slide off. The sky goes orange, then pink, then the colour of a good decision.
It is happening right now. Look. If you are high enough, it looks back.
It is not going anywhere. Well. It is going down. But it comes back.

crab_raver.t: Shh. Listen. Under the bass there is a second bass. That is the crabs. They have been raving on this beach since before the festival, before the road, before the Portuguese.
Four of them run it: Crabcake, Lobsterlad, Ketacrab and Wonkrab. Get all four in your Journal and come back. I will open the floor.
Crabcake, Lobsterlad, Ketacrab, Wonkrab. All four, or the floor stays shut. Crabs are strict about the guest list.
You have all four? All four! Get them out here. Clear the sand. It is time.
Claws up! Sideways! No, the other sideways!
The crabs dance until the tide comes in. Nobody films it. It is better that way.
You have earned this. Hand-sewn from a lilo and two oven gloves. Wear it with pride.
The suit is gone? The tide takes things. So do people.
Hold still. I sewed a spare from the other lilo. The crabs insisted.
Still hearing it? The second bass? Good. Once you hear it, you never stop.

mantequilla.t: Somebody is crouched in the bamboo, picking mushrooms into a basket and humming. There is a guitarron on his back, bigger than he is.
Shh. Shhh. Don't move, amigo. You'll thcare the mutthroomth.
Thethe ones are good. Thethe ones are... lithening. Thethe ones are lithening TO ME.
Ah. Thorry. Mantequilla. Mantequilla el Mexicano. From Vicchio, in Tuthcany. Yeth, I know. It ith a long thtory and the mutthroomth are tired of it.
I drove all the way down here, bimbo. Thix thouthand kilometreth in a Fiat Panda. My nonno thwore it: every year, the alienth of Vicchio follow the rave.
They thpeak in mycelium. They thing in thquare waveth. The thky ith a thieve and they drip through the holeth, one drop, two drop, a drop that ith a door...
...anyway.
You are not on the right frequency. I can thee it in your eyeth. Too thober. Like a tourithtt in the Duomo.
Come back when you are Peaking, amigo. Then we talk about the Vicchio onth.
Thtill too thober, amigo. Peaking. P, E, A, K... the retht of the letterth ecthape me.
The mutthroomth agree with me. They alwayth agree with me. It ith why I like them.
Oh! Oh, look at you. Your pupilth are like two thatellite dithheth. NOW we can talk.
The alienth of Vicchio do not land for anybody. They anthwer a thignal: three Glowing Capth, in a circle, under the thtarth.
The capth only grow for people who are high. Thober people walk right over them. Like tourithtth over a fretheo.
Take thith. My nonno'th antenna. It crackleth when a cap ith near, and I can talk to you through it. Do not athk how. I do not know how.
One at a time, amigo. The capth are shy. When you find one, the antenna will tell you the next.
The first cap... I thee it. Eggth. Thmoke. A man flipping thomething at dawn, very theriouth about it.
The Omelette Thtall, amigo. The north-eatht corner, where nobody queueth.
The capth, amigo. The capth! Let me lithen to the bamboo...
The first cap... I thee it. Eggth. Thmoke. A man flipping thomething at dawn, very theriouth about it.
The Omelette Thtall, amigo. The north-eatht corner, where nobody queueth.
And be Peaking when you get there, or you will thee nothing but eggth.
One cap! It hummth in your pocket. I can hear it from here. The next one...
The thecond one... ith dark there. Very dark. Big thpeakerth breathing in the jungle.
The Forest Stage. The thouth-eatht corner, patht the big mutthroom. Bring a light, or be one.
Two capth! Two! The thecond one thmellth of thubwoofer. Now the latht...
The latht one... water. Thtill water. A lake that ith thweet, like my nonna'th vin thanto.
Sweetwater Lake, on the eatht shore, where the lake pointth at the thky.
Three capth! But look at thith thky. Thun everywhere. The alienth of Vicchio do not like the thun, it maketh them thweaty.
Come back after dark, amigo. Theven o'clock, when the moon comth out to dance.
Three capth. Night. You, high ath a kite. It ith time, amigo.
Mantequilla lays the caps in a triangle on the ground. One after the other, they brighten.
Now... the thignal.
He swings the guitarron round and plays three notes. Low. Lower. Lowest. The bamboo leans in to listen.
VICCHIO! Thiamo qui! We are HERE!
Something hums above the bamboo. A light comes down, green and very patient.
Nonno... Nonno, you were right. Nonno, you were RIGHT!
The light settles somewhere past the bamboo, to the east. The canes part like a curtain. There is a path there that was not there before.
Go, amigo. Through the bamboo. They came for uth both, but I am thcared, and you are the one with the baggieth.
Oh, and take thith. My thombrero. If they athk, you are from Vicchio.
Your thombrero! Gone? Thomebody thtole it off your thleeping head? Ay, amigo.
Lucky for you, a man from Vicchio alwayth carrieth a thpare. Under the guitarron. Do not athk.
They are there, in the crop circle, eatht through the bamboo. Only at night, and only for the Peaking.
Bring me a photo. No. Do not bring me a photo. They hate photoh. It thtealth their thoul. Or ourth. One of the thoulth.
You bagged one? A Vicchiomorph, in your little journal?
Nonno would have cried. I am crying. It ith partly the mutthroomth.
When you thee Tuthcany on a map, amigo, wave. Thomething will wave back.

vicchio_cap1.t: A cluster of mushrooms, glowing softly green. Nobody else seems to notice them.
*krzzt* ...amigo? You found it! I can feel it from here. It tickleth my teeth.
The thecond one... ith dark there. Very dark. Big thpeakerth breathing in the jungle.
The Forest Stage. The thouth-eatht corner, patht the big mutthroom. Bring a light, or be one.

vicchio_cap2.t: A cluster of mushrooms, glowing softly green. Nobody else seems to notice them.
*krzzt* Two! Two capth! My antenna ith dancing. Lithen, the latht one...
The latht one... water. Thtill water. A lake that ith thweet, like my nonna'th vin thanto.
Sweetwater Lake, on the eatht shore, where the lake pointth at the thky.

vicchio_cap3.t: A cluster of mushrooms, glowing softly green. Nobody else seems to notice them.
*krzzt* THREE! Amigo, that ith all of them! Bring them to me in the bamboo.
At night, eh? After theven. The alienth do not like the thun.

sign_crop.t: Wheat, flattened in perfect circles. Nobody grows wheat in Goa.
In daylight it is just a field. A very tidy field.
Something hums in the middle of the circle. You can feel it in your fillings.

vicchiomorph.t: A pocket-sized saucer hovers over the middle of the circle. Something lanky sits in it, and waves at you with one long arm.
Its eyes are very big and very black, and there are stars in them.
The saucer zips up into the stars. It will be back tomorrow night. It likes it here.
The saucer drifts off, empty. Somewhere in Tuscany, a nonno smiles in his sleep.
You back away. It waves again, slower. It has come a long way. It can wait.

inner_door.t: The turning pattern has stopped turning. It is holding itself open, like a door somebody is waiting behind.
Inside, it is very quiet. Even your thoughts take their shoes off.

inner_teacher.t: Oh. Someone came through. Sit, sit. The floor is the only furniture, and it is very comfortable.
I taught the one who sits in the cave out there. Baba Smoke, he calls himself now. He was a skinny boy with a lot of questions and no shoes.
He thinks the teaching is the smoke. The teaching is the room. You cannot carry the room out with you, so take what is on the floor instead.
When you come down, the room folds up. Do not be sad about it. It folds up inside you as well.
Still here? Good. Nobody is ever in a hurry in here. That is the only rule.

mirror_beach.t: Oh. Hi. So that is what I look like from out here.
Shall we find out which one of us is real?
Same moves. Same everything. See you around. I always do.
Your reflection shimmers and is gone. Your Astrals look exactly as they did before. Did that happen?
Fair. I would avoid me too.

mirror_trail.t: Oh. Hi. So that is what I look like from out here.
Shall we find out which one of us is real?
Same moves. Same everything. See you around. I always do.
Your reflection shimmers and is gone. Your Astrals look exactly as they did before. Did that happen?
Fair. I would avoid me too.

memory_vendor.t: A stall that was not here a minute ago. The sign says: MEMORIES, 50 RUPEES. USED.
Memories! Gently used! This one is a sunrise. This one is somebody laughing at a joke you made.
Wait. You look familiar. Have we met? Have I been you?
He bursts into a rainbow. Bits of other people's memories rain down on the market. None of them are yours.

banyan_timetable.t: Somebody is jogging towards you, waving a crumpled piece of paper over his head. It is Banyan, out of breath and very pleased with himself.
Three wristbands! Then you are ready for the real festival. The one that happens at night, and at dawn, and at five in the morning.
Here. The timetable. Every set worth seeing, where and when. Sets bring crowds, and crowds bring Astrals you will not see at any other time.
Check it any time: Sets, in your Fanny Pack. And if you are early for something, any Chai Tent will let you sleep until it starts.
The sunrise set on my beach is at six. I go every morning. I am waiting for someone. Do not ask.

banyan_sunrise.t: Shh. Look at it. Thirty years, and it is still the best set of the day.
Somebody once told me to wait for them at the sunrise set. So here I am. It is a nice place to wait.

gong_player.t: Bonnnnnng. Feel that in your sternum? That is your ego, packing a small bag.
Dance however you want. Nobody is looking. Well. Svetlana is looking. She is always looking.

night_vendor.t: Psst. Night prices, night stock. Things the day vendors are too scared to sell.
I am here until eight. Then I was never here.

stream_cam.t: Shh, we are live! Forty thousand people are watching this sunset. Through Chloe. Who is watching her phone.
Could you step out of shot? You are blocking the sea. And the brand partner.

pit_mc.t: IS THE PIT READY? I SAID, IS THE PIT READY? Diabolo is on the decks until one, and he is taking challengers!
Only during the set, mind. After one he goes back to being a man who will not look at you.

uv_painter.t: Hold still. There. Now you glow under the blacklight. Do not ask what is in the paint.
Darkpsy hour is when the forest shows its real face. Most of it is teeth. Lovely teeth.

queue_raver.t: Is this the queue for omelettes or the queue for the queue? I have been in it since 5 AM. It is still 5 AM.
Raju says one egg per person. I have had four. I think I am four people.

pit_poi.t: Careful, the edge of the stage is ours. Two balls of fire, one hundred and forty-five beats a minute, zero insurance.

yurt_acolyte2.t: Sit on a cushion, any cushion. Not that one. That one is the Guru's. They are all the Guru's.

shrine_keeper.t: The cow on the road? That is Lakshmi. She lies there because the road is warm. Nobody tells a goddess to move.
The jungle way is for people who like mosquitoes. My gate is for people who like being asked for money by a man in sunglasses.
And every morning there are fresh marigolds on the shrine, before I wake up. Seventy years. I have stopped asking. You could ask. Somebody must know.
Lakshmi came in off the road and lay down in the corner. She likes the shade. I like the company.
Before dawn? In the garden? In my nightdress? Picking marigolds... Oh.
Seventy years I thought the goddess was sending them. It was me, sending them to the goddess. That is better, I think. Do not tell the pilgrim. She will want to walk round me.
You let me finish. My mother always said never wake a sleepwalker, they might be busy. Take this. It was hers.
So that is why I woke up in the garden, holding a marigold and shouting at a stranger. I thought it was a dream. It was you.
Seventy years of mystery and you clap in my ear. Well. Now I know. Here, for your trouble. Mine was worse.
I left a note on the shrine for my sleeping self: ALSO WATER THE GARDEN. We will see if she reads it.

sign_jungle.t: JUNGLE SHORTCUT. It is not shorter. It comes out at the top of the road, past the cow. Mind the stream.

sign_shrine.t: ROADSIDE SHRINE. Pilgrims welcome. The path round the shrine comes out at the top of the road. Shoes off in the courtyard. Cows have right of way.

tour_leader.t: Hiya! Fergus, Gap Year Adventures. Twelve countries, nine weeks, one laminated itinerary.
I had seven in my group this morning. I have four. Saskia, Jonas and Tim went into the jungle to find themselves, and the jungle has not given them back.
If you are going through anyway, send them back this way? They will not come quietly. Nobody on this tour does anything quietly.
Still short. Saskia has a ukulele, Jonas has a hammock, and Tim has opinions. You will know them when you hear them.
All three! Muddy, bitten and sunburnt, but all three. Head office need never know.
Here, the group whip-round. And this flask was meant for the best-behaved member of the tour. Frankly, none of them qualify.
Next stop is a silent retreat in the hills. I give it four minutes.

back_saskia.t: I wrote a song about the jungle. It has one chord. The jungle has one chord too, if you listen.

back_jonas.t: My hammock is still up there. I am leaving it for the next guy. That is my legacy, man.

back_tim.t: For the record, I found my own way back. You were just walking in front of me.

shrine_sleeper.t: An old woman in a nightdress, eyes shut, is picking marigolds one at a time in the dark and threading them onto a string.
The old woman from the shrine, in her nightdress, eyes shut, picking marigolds one at a time and threading them onto a string without looking.
Mmm... for Lakshmi... the yellow ones... not by the step, the snail likes those...
You step back onto the path. She finishes the string, pats it, and pads off towards the steps, still asleep, still humming.
You clap. She jumps, stares at the marigolds, stares at you, and says a word that is not in any prayer.
WHO ARE YOU? WHY AM I IN THE GARDEN? Go away! I am in my nightdress!

shrine_pujari.t: Namaste. You came the long way round, because of Lakshmi. Everybody does. Fourteen buses this morning.

She lies on the road because nobody has made her an offering since they tarred it. A green coconut, broken on these steps, and she will get up. That is the tradition. I made it up this morning, but it is a tradition now.
There are coconut palms on the Jungle Shortcut, past the fourth bend. I would go myself, but I am needed here. For sitting.
A green coconut! From the jungle! Give it here.
He lifts it over his head and brings it down on the shrine step. CRACK. Coconut water runs down the stone, and somewhere out on the road a bell on a cow's neck rings once.
Hooves, slow, coming closer. A cow walks in through the gate, past you, and lies down in the corner of the courtyard with a sigh, as if this had been the plan all along.
The road is open, my friend. Tell the bus drivers. Do not tell anyone it was a coconut. Let them think it was me.
Lakshmi's blessing settles over your Astrals. Every one of them feels better.
Lakshmi prefers the courtyard. Cooler in the day, and the old woman brings her marigolds. The road misses her. The buses do not.
